text:
yuki: quick sync — i ran an A/B on the adaptive-coalesce heuristic for host staging vs baseline reclamation. short thread with measurements, weird edgecases, and proposed API boundary.

marie: outline the experiment and results?

yuki: setup: 3-node canary, mixed tenants, 48h run. baseline = opportunistic per-page reclaim + background compactor every 60s. variant = adaptive-coalesce that groups hot adjacent slots into "soft-chunks" and prefers coalesced demote/evict when chunk compactness > 0.7.

sam: what metrics moved?

yuki: p50 unchanged, p95 improved by ~6ms on embedding-heavy tenants, host memory peak dropped ~30MiB per node (median), fragmented free-run increased (fewer small holes), and NVMe spill count fell ~18%. downside: small-model tail (peak <4MB) saw slight p95 regressions ~+9ms.

tia: surprised about NVMe drop. Does coalescing reduce write amplification?

yuki: it does — by batching demotes we avoid many small spill writes and enable larger sequential flushes which the kernel/driver handles more efficiently. also fewer bounce pages during compaction.

marie: how intrusive is the heuristic? is it an allocator change or a routing hint?

yuki: allocator-level with optional hint inputs. core change: we add a compactness score per free-run (stored as a 16-bit fixed-point) and a policy layer that decides whether to coalesce adjacent free-runs into a soft-chunk. there is a small sideband metadata (2 bytes / slot) for run-length encoding of chunk boundaries.

sam: 2 bytes per slot — what's the overhead at scale?

yuki: measured ~3.2% host-mem overhead for our canary configs (slot=32KB). tradeoff: that overhead translated to fewer evictions and less NVMe io. need Econ to validate.

tia: concurrency: compactor and eviction path will race on chunk formation. how are you making it atomic?

yuki: chunk creation happens under an allocation-snapshot epoch. evict path consults snapshot; if it sees a chunk-id mismatch, it falls back to individual page eviction. we used sequence numbers (64-bit epoch) to keep fast-path reads lock-free.

marie: edgecase: when a high-priority tenant causes preemption across a chunk that contains pages from multiple tenants — does coalescing break isolation?

yuki: important point. design ensures chunks are tenant-scoped; we never coalesce across tenant boundaries. for multi-tenant pages mapped to shared model caches we require explicit shared-chunk opt-in via the hint API.

sam: what's the hint API look like?

yuki: lean proto: {slot_index, desired_chunk_id (optional), allow_shared: bool, priority_hint: enum}. idea is the compiler or caching layer can suggest chunk candidates. runtime may accept, ignore, or coalesce differently.

tia: ops question: how do we detect harmful coalescing (e.g., causing small-model tails to regress)?

yuki: added compactness_ratio gauge per-tenant and a small-model_detector (rolling 10m footprint estimate). alert rule proposed: if tenant compactness_ratio > 0.8 AND small_model_detector == true for >3m, trigger auto-fallback to per-page reclaim for that tenant.

marie: auto-fallback across mixed nodes could cause coordination issues. do we demote tenant config centrally?

yuki: yes we use config-service flags per-tenant. fallback flips a tenant-scoped flag; nodes observe via usual config refresh. to avoid oscillation we add 2-window confirmation and 10m cooldown.

sam: rollback plan for canary or prod?

yuki: canary: immediate config flip + kill switch on rollout. prod: staged rollout with progressive percentage and circuit-breaker (rate of spill errors and tail latency). if the breaker trips we revert via config and rotate nodes through restart-free rollout.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: adaptive-coalesce:v3 on cluster canary-7  2026-03-23T11:05:01Z

tia: any instrumentation we should add before wider rollout?

yuki: yes: per-tenant compactness_histogram, chunk_size_distribution, spill_write_size_histogram, and chunk_conflict_rate. also a debug flag to force-chunk-id for deterministic repro.

ops-bot: note recorded: add playbook steps to identify coalescing regressions (how to query compactness_ratio and recent spill sizes).

marie: one more thing — can we make the chunk policy adaptive to thermal/IO pressure? when NVMe is saturated maybe fall back to aggressive coalesce to reduce small writes.

yuki: we prototyped an IO-pressure adapter: it favors larger chunks when smoothed_io_bandwidth > 80%. early tests show reduced write ops but slightly larger latency variance. I'd like to bake that into policy toggles rather than default.

sam: sounds good. next actions?

yuki: 1) cost model run (dollars saved vs metadata overhead), 2) add suggested telemetry and playbook, 3) formalize hint proto + RFC appendix on epoch semantics, 4) run a 7d canary with IO-pressure adapter enabled on half nodes. ping @marie @tia for review on the RFC. :rocket:
